table.name: Addresses
table.purpose: A lookup/parent table of postal addresses (street lines, city, state/province/county, country, ZIP/postcode), each identified by address_id. Students reference these addresses via permanent_address_id and current_address_id, so each row represents one address used as a student's permanent and/or current residence. The data appears synthetic (fictional city names, mismatched countries and US states, 3-digit ZIP codes).

address_id.name: address_id
address_id.description: Primary key of the Addresses table; unique identifier for each address record. Referenced by Students.permanent_address_id and Students.current_address_id.

city.name: city
city.description: City name of the address. All values are unique in this small sample, but that is incidental.

line_1.name: line_1
line_1.description: First street line of the address (street number, street name, optionally unit designator).

line_2.name: line_2
line_2.description: Second address line, holding apartment/suite designators (e.g. 'Apt. 388', 'Suite 703').

state_province_county.name: state_province_county
state_province_county.description: State, province, or county of the address. Values are mostly US state names (some written without spaces, e.g. 'SouthDakota', 'NorthCarolina'), though the paired countries are international — likely synthetic/inconsistent test data.

zip_postcode.name: zip_postcode
zip_postcode.description: Postal/ZIP code of the address. Stored as text (leading zeros preserved, e.g. '068'); values are 3-digit codes, so likely synthetic rather than real postal codes.

table.name: Courses
table.purpose: Catalog of courses offered by the institution; each row is one course with a unique ID and name, referenced by the Sections and Student_Enrolment_Courses tables. Part of a student records database (Students, Transcripts, Semesters, Departments, Degree_Programs, etc.).

course_description.name: course_description
course_description.description: Free-text description of the course. Values in this dataset are single letters (e.g. 'q', 'l', 'p'), likely placeholder/test data, so the actual content is uninformative; the column's role as a descriptive text field is supported by its name and type.

course_id.name: course_id
course_id.description: Primary key of the Courses table; unique integer identifier for each course (1-15). Referenced by Student_Enrolment_Courses.course_id and Sections.course_id, which associate enrolments and course sections with their course.

course_name.name: course_name
course_name.description: Name/title of the course, unique per row. Values are short abbreviations of academic subjects: 'ai' (artificial intelligence), 'cal' (calculus), 'db' (databases), 'dl' (deep learning), 'ds' (data structures), 'nlp' (natural language processing), 'fr' (French), 'math' (mathematics), 'la' (linear algebra), 'os' (operating systems), 'en' (English).

table.name: Degree_Programs
table.purpose: Catalog of degree programs offered by the institution, each belonging to a department and classified by degree level (Bachelor/Master/PHD), with a short description. Referenced by Student_Enrolment to indicate which program a student is enrolled in.

degree_program_id.name: degree_program_id
degree_program_id.description: Primary key of the degree program; unique integer identifier for each program row.

degree_summary_description.name: degree_summary_description
degree_summary_description.description: Free-text description of the degree program. Values are placeholder/lorem-style words (e.g. 'aperiam', 'architecto'), so the actual semantic content is dummy data, but the column's role as a descriptive text field is clear.

degree_summary_name.name: degree_summary_name
degree_summary_name.description: Degree level of the program: Bachelor, Master, or PHD.

department_id.name: department_id
department_id.description: Foreign key to Departments.department_id; the department offering the degree program.

table.name: Departments
table.purpose: Lookup table of academic departments at an educational institution. Each row is one department with a unique id and name, referenced by Degree_Programs to link degree programs to their owning department. The description column contains placeholder (Lorem-ipsum-style) text, indicating the data is synthetic/test data. The other_details column is entirely null and its purpose is unknown.

department_description.name: department_description
department_description.description: Free-text description of the department. Values are Latin placeholder words (e.g. 'consequatur', 'nihil'), suggesting dummy/test data rather than real descriptions.

department_id.name: department_id
department_id.description: Primary key of the Departments table; unique integer identifier for each academic department (1-15). Referenced by Degree_Programs.department_id, which assigns each degree program to a department.

department_name.name: department_name
department_name.description: Name of the academic department (e.g. 'computer science', 'biology', 'math', 'history'). Unique across the 15 rows.

table.name: Sections
table.purpose: One row per course section (an offering/instance of a course, e.g. 'Section A'), linked to its parent course via course_id and referenced by enrolment/transcript tables.

course_id.name: course_id
course_id.description: Foreign key to Courses.course_id identifying the course this section belongs to; a course can have multiple sections (many-to-one).

section_description.name: section_description
section_description.description: Free-text description of the section (sample values are placeholder Latin words, so only the text role is evident).

section_id.name: section_id
section_id.description: Primary key of the Sections table; unique identifier for each course section.

section_name.name: section_name
section_name.description: Short label distinguishing sections of the same course (single letters a, b, c, ...), like 'Section A'.

table.name: Semesters
table.purpose: Lookup table of academic semesters/terms (e.g. 'spring 2018', 'fall 2010'), one row per semester, keyed by semester_id and referenced by student enrolment records to indicate which semester an enrolment belongs to.

semester_id.name: semester_id
semester_id.description: Primary key of the Semesters table; integer 1-15, one row per semester. Referenced by Student_Enrolment.semester_id (many enrolments per semester).

semester_name.name: semester_name
semester_name.description: Human-readable semester label in the form '<term> <year>', e.g. 'spring 2018', 'fall 2010', 'summer 2010', 'winter 2010'. Nearly unique (one duplicate, 'spring 2018'), covering roughly 2010-2019.

table.name: Student_Enrolment
table.purpose: Records each enrolment of a student into a degree program for a specific semester; links students to degree programs and semesters, and is referenced by Student_Enrolment_Courses which holds the courses taken within each enrolment.

degree_program_id.name: degree_program_id
degree_program_id.description: Foreign key to Degree_Programs.degree_program_id; the degree program in which the student is enrolled for that semester.

semester_id.name: semester_id
semester_id.description: Foreign key to Semesters.semester_id; the academic term of the enrolment.

student_enrolment_id.name: student_enrolment_id
student_enrolment_id.description: Primary key; one row per student enrolment record (a student's enrolment in a degree program for a given semester).

student_id.name: student_id
student_id.description: Foreign key to Students.student_id; the enrolled student. A student can appear in multiple enrolment rows (e.g. across semesters or programs).

table.name: Student_Enrolment_Courses
table.purpose: Junction table linking a student's enrolment (Student_Enrolment) to the individual courses (Courses) taken under that enrolment; each row is one course within one student enrolment, and its records are referenced by transcript contents.

course_id.name: course_id
course_id.description: Foreign key to Courses.course_id; identifies the course the student is enrolled in for this enrolment record.

student_course_id.name: student_course_id
student_course_id.description: Primary key of this table; unique identifier for a student-course enrolment record. Referenced by Transcript_Contents.student_course_id, linking enrolments to transcript entries. The mixed small and large values suggest a surrogate key from different sources or a merged dataset.

student_enrolment_id.name: student_enrolment_id
student_enrolment_id.description: Foreign key to Student_Enrolment.student_enrolment_id; identifies the student's overall enrolment (e.g. per semester/program) to which this course belongs.

table.name: Students
table.purpose: One row per student: personal identity (names, SSN, contact details), registration/leaving dates, and links to current and permanent addresses. Students are enrolled via the Student_Enrolment table.

cell_mobile_number.name: cell_mobile_number
cell_mobile_number.description: Student's mobile phone number, stored as free-formatted text with inconsistent styles (dashes, dots, parentheses, extensions).

current_address_id.name: current_address_id
current_address_id.description: Foreign key to Addresses.address_id — the student's current (term-time) address.

date_first_registered.name: date_first_registered
date_first_registered.description: Timestamp when the student first registered at the institution. Stored as text but parses as a datetime.

date_left.name: date_left
date_left.description: Timestamp when the student left the institution (graduated or withdrew). Stored as text but parses as a datetime. Note: sample rows show date_left earlier than date_first_registered, so the data appears synthetic/corrupted; the semantic meaning is still 'date the student left'.

email_address.name: email_address
email_address.description: Student's email address (unique per row in this sample).

other_student_details.name: other_student_details
other_student_details.description: Free-text catch-all field for miscellaneous student details. Values are random Latin-like filler words (e.g. 'omnis', 'atque'), so no real semantic content is discernible beyond 'unstructured extra details'.

permanent_address_id.name: permanent_address_id
permanent_address_id.description: Foreign key to Addresses.address_id — the student's permanent (home) address.

ssn.name: ssn
ssn.description: Student's Social Security Number, stored as text. Values are inconsistent (empty strings, 1–3 digit numbers, one 9-digit value), so the data quality is poor, but the column is clearly intended as the SSN identifier.

student_id.name: student_id
student_id.description: Primary key of the Students table; unique numeric identifier for each student. Referenced by Student_Enrolment.student_id.

table.name: Transcript_Contents
table.purpose: Junction/association table linking a student's transcript (Transcripts) to the individual enrolled courses (Student_Enrolment_Courses) that appear on it. Each row states that a given student-course enrolment is included in a given transcript; the table itself carries no additional attributes.

student_course_id.name: student_course_id
student_course_id.description: Foreign key to Student_Enrolment_Courses.student_course_id — identifies the specific course a student took within an enrolment. Values are mostly small integers (0–96) with occasional large IDs (e.g. 70882679), suggesting mixed ID generation; the meaning of the row is unaffected.

transcript_id.name: transcript_id
transcript_id.description: Foreign key to Transcripts.transcript_id — the transcript this course record belongs to.

table.name: Transcripts
table.purpose: One row per academic transcript issued to a student, identified by transcript_id and dated by transcript_date. The detailed contents (courses, grades, credits) live in the child table Transcript_Contents, which joins on transcript_id. The other_details column is a nullable tagged-union catch-all that is unused in this dataset. Note: no direct link to Students is observed in this table's columns, so the owning student is presumably resolved through Transcript_Contents or another relationship not visible here.

transcript_date.name: transcript_date
transcript_date.description: Timestamp of when the transcript was issued/created, stored as a VARCHAR but containing datetime values (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS). Ranges from 1975 to 2013; unique per row, so each transcript has its own date. The wide, seemingly random spread of dates suggests synthetic or randomly generated data rather than real issuance dates.

transcript_id.name: transcript_id
transcript_id.description: Primary key of the Transcripts table; a surrogate integer identifier (1–15, one per row). Referenced by Transcript_Contents.transcript_id, which holds the per-course line items belonging to each transcript.
